extracted.intended_audience: scientists and naturalists (museum curators, textbook authors, astronomers, statisticians, anatomists) / readers of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for a range of scientific communications and practices presented in book reviews and letters (museum display, textbooks, conference organization, statistical analysis, anatomical identification, and interpretation of Mendelian claims). Useful for reviewers, editors, and practitioners assessing quality and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen display principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens should not be crowded together; each should be exhibited with a purpose, instructively or 'descriptively' labelled, and placed so that it can be properly seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid indiscriminate taxidermy in cases; prioritize instructive presentation over mere accumulation of specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of series versus labelled collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how far the principle of making a popular series rather a collection of 'labels ... illustrated by specimens' than a collection of specimens explained by labels should be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators must choose the proper balance between pictorial/pedagogic mounting and pure specimen display; extent of 'pictorial mounting' is a matter for considered judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pictorial mounting in museums
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of how far 'pictorial mounting' ought to be adopted in natural history museums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh educational benefit against potential loss of specimen-focused scientific display; decision depends on museum mission and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook scope appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: A textbook intended as a first-year course for students of not very high scholastic attainments should not 'cover too much ground.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading introductory courses; do not expect novices to master an excessive breadth (example: starting from elementary experiments then covering dynamos, alternators, lighting circuits, measuring instruments, primary cells, accumulators in one prelim course is inadvisable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical sympathy with manufacturing in technical texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of engineering texts should display 'closer sympathy' with manufacturing practice and avoid conveying naive or misleading examples about industry practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wasteful or ridiculous manufacturing examples in textbooks (example: treating a wooden block in a dry cell as an 'economy in first cost' is a travesty); emphasize economically sensible, realistic engineering practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic completeness and problem selection in instructional works
rubrics_metrics.description: An instructional book (e.g., on spherical trigonometry and globe usage) should trace history, indicate principal problems for mechanical solution, show forms of apparatus (orrery), exhibit considerable ingenuity in choice and variety of problems, give many examples to be worked by the student, and indicate methods of solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good instructional volume is notable for completeness, suitability for novices, variety of exercises, and explanatory solutions; include apparatus suggestions to approach accuracy where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and appropriate technical level
rubrics_metrics.description: A survey book (e.g., on modern hygiene) should be interesting, readable, and non-technical while being appropriately targeted; some chapters may belong in more technical medical texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content into clear sections (individual, home, community, public hygiene); avoid extreme one-sided positions; tailor depth to intended readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/programme organisation for observational sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sufficient time and appropriate sectional structure for outdoor/observational subjects (terrestrial magnetism, atmospheric electricity, seismology, meteorology) which cannot be pursued adequately within a laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider restoring subsections (e.g., 'Astronomy and Cosmical Physics' / geophysics subsection), appoint at least one special secretary, schedule papers at accessible times, and print important opening papers in extenso when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate statistical measures (correlation coefficient vs correlation ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose statistical measures suited to the theoretical relationship: the correlation coefficient may hide relationships when the true relation is non-linear (e.g., logarithmic), and the correlation ratio may be more appropriate in such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume one measure fits all; examine regression curve shape (sinuosities, quartic possibilities) and select measures that reflect underlying theory and data behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate and rule out selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming that observed features (e.g., 'humps' in a parallax-magnitude curve) arise from selection by a third variable (e.g., proper motion), you must show (i) the third variable is highly correlated with the primary variables, (ii) selection concentrated at particular ranges, and (iii) that selection could produce the observed effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on visual impressions or selective examples; provide logical demonstration and quantitative checks that selection bias explains the observation rather than random sampling or outliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for sampling variability and influence of individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: With small or subdivided samples, averages of subclasses are 'largely influenced by individuals'; statisticians call this the result of random sampling and expect consideration of probable errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess effect of outliers (e.g., removing one star changes correlation greatly), report probable errors and show whether differences are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct measures (components vs totals) when computing correlations
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that correlations computed on components of a vector quantity (e.g., proper motion components) differ systematically from correlations on the total magnitude; theoretical relationships exist between them (e.g., multiplying factor 2/(1+r)^1 where r is mutual correlation of components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form of the measurement (total proper motion versus components) for comparisons and be explicit about transformations and their effects on correlation values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset inclusion/exclusion should be physically justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions to include or exclude classes of objects (e.g., 'white' stars) must be justified by physical reasoning; inclusion/exclusion can materially affect correlation values and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results with and without such subclasses; if exclusion is made, explain physical grounds (e.g., white stars have similar mean magnitude and no place on a luminosity-colour scale) and show the effect on statistical measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret suggestive patterns with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid drawing far-reaching conclusions from vague suggestions or incomplete data; 'a suggestion, even if it be only of the vaguest kind,' should not be taken as definitive without robust evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm suggestive patterns across datasets, consider alternative explanations (selection, sampling), and avoid overstating implications for the general system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for anatomical sex and age determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex and age of human skeletal remains are determined by characteristic features: skull (size, heavy jaw, frontal sinuses, superciliary ridges, mastoid processes), pelvis (shape of pubes, pubo-ischial rami, subpubic angle, obturator foramen, pelvic cavity proportions, iliac bones), femur (size, inclination, head), tooth wear and eruption (wisdom teeth status), and state of epiphyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple concordant skeletal indicators; presence of unworn teeth and ununited epiphyses indicate youth (~25 years), while pelvic and cranial morphology indicate sex (male vs female). Photographic documentation and comparative analysis strengthen conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance and unique treatment as identity evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique treatments or packaging (e.g., bones soaked with paraffin wax and known packing/unpacking chain) can establish identity and provenance of specimens or finds beyond reasonable doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document chain of custody and any unique physical treatments as part of the identification record; this supports claims about origin/identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific openness and method adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The first introduction of modern statistical methods into an established field may be met with scorn, but practitioners should remain open; early critics may later tacitly adopt the methods they initially contemn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage measured critique and willingness to learn methods (e.g., modern statistics) rather than dismissing new approaches out of hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of Mendelian phenomena and definition of 'bi-parental'
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement 'Mendelian phenomena are possible only when reproduction is bi-parental' should be interpreted flexibly: 'bi-parental' need not be literal, since many Mendelian studies use self-fertilisation (autogamy); experimental evidence is required before declaring phenomena impossible in particular reproductive modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-literal definitions; seek experimental confirmation before accepting theoretical impossibilities regarding inheritance modes.
